author: kaxelsen
body:
I did not annotate this paper, so I don't know. Normally, we only include activities that happens at >10% of the highest activity, except for when such a reaction is important for the survival of the organism and there are no other enzymes doing it. In this case it seems both reactions are involved in arginine biosynthesis, so both reactions might be relevant for the yeasts.
I suggest you ask @marcfeuermann whether he knows more about the subject.

author: ValWood
body: Hi @marcfeuermann what do you think? The paper that is used to assign GO:0004042 | L-glutamate N-acetyltransferase activity (acetylglutamate synthase activity) to pombe aga1, cerevisiae ARG7 is 0.3 % of S. cerevisiae ARG2 (at least PMID: 9428669 was the only paper I could find, and they make a big deal of this secondary activity in the title) but

author: ValWood
body: Also ARG2 is arginine requiring, so ARG7 can't substitute for ARG2 in vivo.

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Hello,
I'm not familiar with these specific papers or entries, and above all I'm not involved in HAMAP.  However, I'm not going to hand over the hot potato to another unfortunate person without checking what's happening here.
The corresponding HAMAP rule is https://www.uniprot.org/unirule/UR000106930
It is based on the _S.cerevisiae_ entry **Q04728** and the _Citrullus lanatus_ enty **Q3C251**, which means **PMID:9428669** and **PMID:16218965**
I do not see any mention to the second reaction in PMID:16218965.

The problems comes from the yeast paper. The kind of papers I hate since you do not clearly understand what the authors want to explain.
**Abstract**
"We have addressed the question of the bifunctionality of the eucaryotic enzyme, showing that overexpressed ARG7 can complement yeast arg2 and Escherichia coli argA mutations (affecting acetylglutamate synthase). Furthermore, Arg7p-linked acetylglutamate synthase activity was measurable in an assay. **The yeast enzyme is thus clearly, albeit modestly, bifunctional**."

This seems quite clear about the double function. It is only later within the text, that you discover that modestly means very very very low... I would say it is "clearly" too modest to be considered as a function of this enzyme. So I would agree to remove the N-acetylglutamate synthase activity from the HAMAP rule and from these proteins in more general. However, this is not one of my areas of expertise and I think we should pass the hot potato on to Ivo.

@pedruzzi, sorry, I think it is your turn to add your two cents ;-)
